_comment: The key every published extension is signed with. It is never stored in the
repository: the fingerprint in repo/repo.json is what identifies this repository,
and a keystore anyone can read would make that worthless, since anyone could then
sign an extension that matches it. It is also not generated by a run: a new key
would change the signature, and Android will not update an installed extension
across a change of signing key.
Instead it is a repository secret, SIGNING_KEY, holding the base64 of a keystore.
Generating one is .github/scripts/new-signing-key.sh. The run refuses to build
without it, because upstream falls back to the debug key when signingkey.jks is
missing - which would publish extensions nobody can update later - so there is no
safe default to fall back on.
The alias and passwords are not the secret (the keystore file is); they default to
these values unless the ALIAS, KEY_STORE_PASSWORD and KEY_PASSWORD secrets are set.
An APK is only published if every gate passes. Tachimanga runs the classic
Mihon/Tachiyomi extension API; extensions compiled against keiyoushi extensions-lib
1.6 (KeiSource) require Mihon 0.20.1+ and fail on Tachimanga.
These are checked on the built APK, so they cannot be fooled by build-config changes.
Tachimanga requires minSdk 21 (that is what its 'Unsupported extension' message
tells you to rebuild with). Upstream raised minSdk to 26 in gradle/kei.versions.toml,
which would make every extension below unloadable, so builds rewrite that value to
this number first, and the gate still rejects anything that ends up above it.

extensions._comment: Upstream moved to libVersion 1.6 / KeiSource on 2026-09-11, so this is pinned to the last revision that still uses the classic API, with the ?verify= image-parsing fix backported onto it.

_comment: A previous build is kept when an extension is replaced, so rolling back is a one-line
index change. This caps how many are kept per extension; publishing a newer one drops
the oldest beyond the cap, so the repository cannot grow without bound.
-1 keeps every previous build (and is what a missing key falls back to).
Checked on every run without building anything, to give early warning about things
that affect us: a module migrating to the incompatible API, a custom source upstream
has since added, or a module we carry disappearing from upstream.
Upstream moves modules between language directories, so these are the paths as they
stand now - src/all/manga18fx was src/en/manga18fx until it changed language.
